goal: Phase 3 (reference-load) of campaign env-independence-and-generated-docs: the set of documents a worker packet may load is declared and guarded, and status and report expose the bytes each node's declared readFiles weigh at dispatch. Spec: docs/campaigns/env-independence-and-generated-docs/spec/SPEC.md.

definitionOfDone.text: the reference-load guard passes on the current fixtures and its unit cases
the worker-loadable set is declared in one exported function and the docs/ refusal has the write-scope exception

taskPacket.objective: test/docs/reference-load.test.mjs declares the worker-loadable reference set (skills/faberun/SKILL.md and skills/faberun/references/*.md) and refuses any fixture contract whose packet readFiles points under docs/ unless the same path is in that packet's writeFiles.
instructions: Evidence: skills/faberun/SKILL.md is 1,002 bytes and routes to six references; nothing stops a packet from putting docs/COMMANDS.md (42 KB) in readFiles and undoing the diet in one line. docs/ is operator documentation; a worker reads it only when it edits it.

Write test/docs/reference-load.test.mjs: (1) `workerReferenceSet()` returns SKILL.md plus every file under skills/faberun/references/, and the test asserts each reference is linked from SKILL.md (the router) and that the directory holds nothing else; (2) walk every contract JSON under evals/fixtures and evals/deterministic (skip evals/golden and docs/campaigns, which are records) and, for each node's taskPacket, assert no readFiles entry starts with docs/ unless writeFiles contains the same path; report file, node and path on failure; (3) a unit test with an inline contract object proving the refusal and the write-scope exception. Introduce `workerReferenceSet` as the declared list's one home.
decisions: A node may read a docs/ file it writes; anything else under docs/ is refused.
Records (evals/golden, docs/campaigns) are never scanned or edited.
nonGoals: No change to src/ or to any fixture contract unless the guard finds one that violates the rule, in which case report it in the summary and leave it for the orchestrator.
No edit to skills/faberun/references/*.md, docs/history/**, docs/campaigns/**, evals/golden/**. CONTRACT_VERSION stays 0.3.0.
No file over 800 lines: when a module or test file you must extend is near the ceiling, add a new module or test file instead of growing it.
Do not run the full suite yourself; the controller runs your verification after you declare done. Quick targeted test files are fine.
No new test bounds a measured duration from above, depends on the wall clock, on a binary in PATH, or on the machine layout: that is the theme of this campaign.

definitionOfDone.text: declared-read-bytes, report and web server tests pass
the snapshot value equals the sizes of the declared files at dispatch and both JSON payloads expose it

taskPacket.objective: At dispatch the controller sums the byte sizes of a node's declared readFiles in the attempt worktree and records declaredReadBytes on the node snapshot; status --json and report --json expose it per node so reference load is measured by declared weight.
instructions: Evidence: the diet is measured today by file sizes in test/docs/docs-diet.test.mjs; nothing reports what a packet actually declared to load. The worker prompt lists readFiles (src/contract/task-packet.mjs renderWorkerPrompt) and the worker reads them itself, so the declared weight is the one quantity the controller can measure.

Change 1, src/engine/dispatch.mjs (where the worker prompt is assembled for an attempt; read it first and, if the workspace path is not available there, use the lifecycle call site that has it): introduce `declaredReadBytes(readFiles, workspace)` returning the sum of statSync sizes of the files that exist (missing files count 0, never throw), and store the number on the node snapshot as `declaredReadBytes` through the existing snapshot write at attempt start.

Change 2, src/report/render.mjs: the status payload's node entries carry declaredReadBytes (number|null); the human table does not gain a column (keep the row width) but the per-node `## Nodes` note or the run's `## Cost` line shows `read <compact bytes>`; src/report/final.mjs's report --json includes it per node and as a run total.

Tests: a new test/engine/declared-read-bytes.test.mjs that dispatches a node with two known readFiles in a temp workspace and asserts the snapshot value equals their sizes (use the fixtures test/engine/sandbox-notice.test.mjs uses); test/report/cost.test.mjs or a new test/report/read-bytes.test.mjs asserting the JSON payload carries the field. Node snapshot fields are not governed by docs/FIELD-OWNERSHIP.md (events.jsonl and journal.jsonl only); do not add an events.jsonl writer.
Docs: one sentence in docs/CONCEPTS.md where reference load or the diet is described.
decisions: Declared weight at dispatch is the measurement; what the worker actually reads is the harness's business.
The field lives on the node snapshot and in the JSON payloads, not in events.jsonl.
nonGoals: No change to lifecycle.mjs (772 lines) unless the workspace path is only available there; if so, the smallest possible edit.
No dashboard change beyond the shared payload.
No edit to skills/faberun/references/*.md, docs/history/**, docs/campaigns/**, evals/golden/**. CONTRACT_VERSION stays 0.3.0.
No file over 800 lines: when a module or test file you must extend is near the ceiling, add a new module or test file instead of growing it.
Do not run the full suite yourself; the controller runs your verification after you declare done. Quick targeted test files are fine.
No new test bounds a measured duration from above, depends on the wall clock, on a binary in PATH, or on the machine layout: that is the theme of this campaign.
